conviction_note: Nothing unpriced and decisive was found: the reported quarter will very likely land at or just above a guide the company has beaten every quarter, so the print turns on a first FY27 guide set against a thin, disputed $1.71-1.76 consensus, into a 16% 20-day run-up with downside paid in an illiquid chain. abs_move is set at 7.0, above the 6.45% implied move, because this is the guidance print (last year's Q4 moved +15.3%). p_up 46 leans slightly down on positioning only. The findings sum to -1.4 and the scaled number is -0.56; the gap is small and both say the same thing: a weak, mostly positioning lean.
bar: Q4 FY26 company guide: net revenue $1.12-1.17bn, EPS $0.45-0.48; FY26 adj. EPS $1.56-1.59, net revenue $4.315-4.365bn (Q3 release, SEC 8-K Ex.99.1 https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/831641/000110465926088213/tm2621536d1_ex99-1.htm, 2026-07-29). Consensus Q4 EPS $0.47 on ~$1.14-1.15bn revenue, two agreeing sources: Earnings Whispers preview via finviz https://finviz.com/news/414950/tetra-tech-must-prove-its-backlog-inflection-is-real-as-shares-test-recent-highs (2026-11-03) and the Investing.com preview https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/tetra-tech-investors-brace-for-earnings-as-revenue-expected-to-slip-93CH-5019381. The FY27 bar, which is the line this print usually trades on, is NOT well sourced: aggregators show $1.71 (stockalarm), $1.74 (Barchart, KeyBanc in April) and $1.76 on 2 analysts. Treat it as disputed, so the guidance findings are capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest 11.88m shares, days to cover 4.8 (shortsqueeze.com, page dated 2026-10-25, https://shortsqueeze.com/?symbol=TTEK). Equibles shows 11.8m shares and 3.7 days at 2026-08-20, falling (https://equibles.com/stocks/ttek/shortinterest). Benzinga shows about 4.8% of float. That is moderate, not a crowded short. Skew from the baseline: +9.49 vol points 25d put over call, 'downside paid'. But the chain is very thin (total OI 624, put/call OI 0.26, ATM spread 52% of mid), so both the skew and the 6.45% event-implied move are indicative only. Tape: +16.19% over 20 days, -4.62% over 5 days, 8.35% below the 52-week high. Spot $39.05 against a mean analyst target of about $40.17 (8 Buy ratings per Investing.com). One unnamed analyst raised its target to $41 on 2026-11-03 (https://www.webull.com/news/15858679256751104). Earnings Whispers bearish sentiment is 22.6%, down from 47.3% a quarter earlier.

findings.finding: The stock goes into the print up 16.19% over 20 days (up about 13% since the Q3 report, roughly 11 points ahead of the S&P), at $39.05 against a mean analyst target of about $40.17. On the last two prints this name sold or barely bought a beat-and-raise: Q3 FY26 (2026-07-29) beat with a FY guide raise and fell 3.94%; Q2 FY26 rose 1.41% after a beat and raise, with profit-taking reported.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Baseline: 2026-07-29 -3.94% after a beat and a fourth straight FY raise; 2026-04-29 +1.41% (rallies.ai: 'slides as traders take profits after Q2 beat and FY2026 guidance raise'); 2026-01-28 +3.02%. Up moves of 12.95% and 15.29% came only on prints that reset the forward view (May 2025, Nov 2025 FY26 first guide).
findings.why_not_priced: Only partly unpriced: the run-up is the market's own bet on a good guide, and the preview itself says an in-line print may not be enough to break resistance near the $39.80 post-earnings high. If the market had fully priced the profit-taking risk, the 20-day run-up would not sit at +16% with the stock at the consensus target. The -4.6% over 5 days shows some of it coming out already.
findings.independence: Agrees with the baseline skew (+9.49, downside paid), though the chain is illiquid. Price-target level from Investing.com (https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/tetra-tech-investors-brace-for-earnings-as-revenue-expected-to-slip-93CH-5019381). Shares the finviz preview with the bar.

findings.finding: Ukraine-related Department of State revenue runs at about $66m a quarter, roughly 6% of net revenue. On the Q3 call the CFO expected Q4 to be similar and the CEO called the long-term level politically uncertain and said the company forecasts it 'conservatively'. A first FY27 guide that assumes a wind-down would hold the growth number down relative to an ex-USAID run-rate of +8%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: USAID/State exposure was the cause of the 2025 drawdowns, and the stock sold off on the USAID cuts (newsquantified). The line has not surprised on a print since the wind-down was guided.
findings.why_not_priced: The exposure is public, but how much of the $264m annualised run-rate FY27 guidance assumes is not. If the market had priced a conservative assumption, the FY27 consensus would sit below the +10% EPS growth that $1.74-1.76 implies.
findings.independence: SPARC Ukraine energy procurement under State Department contracting continued into 2026 (https://www.developmentaid.org/tenders/view/1647410/procurement-of-blok-modular-dual-fuel-gas-diesel-boiler-house-5-mw, 2026-05-05), so the work is live. That cuts against a cliff, and it is why the size is small.

findings.finding: Federal FY27 is funded only by a continuing resolution to 2026-12-11, after what reporting calls two record-long shutdowns in the past year (one of 43 days ended November 2025). A shutdown risk in Q1 FY27 gives management a reason to guide the first half cautiously on its US federal business, which grew double digits in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline print turned explicitly on a shutdown. The Q3 call flagged federal contracting friction (staff cuts, shorter task orders) slowing procurement, and the stock fell 3.94% on that print.
findings.why_not_priced: The deadline is public macro. Whether TTEK embeds a lapse in its guide is not. If it were priced, a federal-heavy engineering name would not trade 20% above its 200-day average into a guide with a funding cliff four weeks into the year. This is a proxy: macro-to-company transmission the company has not confirmed.
findings.independence: SAM Search on 2026-10-17 told contractors to prepare contingency plans for a lapse (https://samsearch.co/government-contracting-news/congress-confronts-uncertainty-over-federal-funding-and-possible-shutdown-219469).

findings.finding: Parsons, a federal counterparty-peer that reported on 2026-10-28, after TTEK last spoke, posted Federal Solutions awards up 53% year on year and a 1.2x book-to-bill for the July-September quarter. That points to the federal fiscal-year-end obligation push unlocking in TTEK's Q4 (TTEK's fiscal Q4 is also July-September), which supports a third straight sequential backlog rise from $4.49bn.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Backlog is the line the preview names as the focus. Q3's +5% sequential backlog rise came with a -3.94% reaction, so a backlog beat has not been paid for by itself recently.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the run-up may already reflect the federal recovery. A peer's bookings number is not in the TTEK preview, which still cites procurement friction. If it were priced, the preview would not frame backlog as something TTEK 'must prove'.
findings.independence: Parsons release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000275880/000119312526435041/psn-ex99_1.htm). Parsons also said protests and procurement timing could delay ramps, which is why the size is small. Proxy: different mix (defense/IT against environmental/water).

findings.finding: WSP's Q3 2026 release (2026-11-04) said the Americas saw 'a more measured pace of project conversion' while Canada and EMEIA posted double-digit growth, and Americas organic backlog growth was 4.9%. Stantec's Q2 had US organic growth flat on deferred public and private capital decisions. Both read as soft US commercial and state/local conversion, where TTEK's US commercial grew only about 1% in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: US commercial weakness (offshore wind cancellations) was cited in the Q3 reaction (-3.94%).
findings.why_not_priced: A peer's regional commentary after TTEK last spoke. It is a proxy, and the TTEK preview does not cite it. If the market had absorbed it, the US-commercial recovery thesis (power, data centers, mining) would not be carrying the run-up.
findings.independence: Stantec Q2 2026 MD&A (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001131383/000113138326000017/ex-991xmdaxq2x2026x6k.htm). It is older, and a different firm.

findings.finding: Hurricane Isaias made landfall as a Category 2 near Destin, Florida on 2026-10-09, the first US hurricane since 2024, leaving more than 1m without power and debris across the Panhandle. TTEK runs FEMA-reimbursed debris monitoring for Gulf counties, so this is episodic revenue that could appear in Q1 FY27 commentary.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None. The company strips episodic disaster work out of its growth figures and guides excluding it.
findings.why_not_priced: Nobody links the storm to TTEK, but the company excludes episodic work from its headline growth, so even a real contribution barely reaches the guide. This is a weather inference, sized tiny.
findings.independence: TTEK's own disaster-debris practice description (https://www.tetratech.com/?p=1217). No document ties TTEK to Isaias.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-10 the board added $500m of buyback authorisation, for $898m available, about 8.8% of a roughly $10.2bn market cap. TTM operating cash flow is $567m, net leverage 0.88x, and 9-month OCF of $467m is a record. That supports EPS-per-share growth in the FY27 guide above the organic rate.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No print turned on capital return. The authorisation was announced between prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the authorisation is public. What is not known is whether FY27 EPS guidance assumes an accelerated pace of about $100m a quarter or more. If guidance includes it, a 3%+ share-count tailwind supports clearing a $1.74-1.76 bar.
findings.independence: Q3 8-K: $100m repurchased in Q3, $202m year to date (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/831641/000110465926088213/tm2621536d1_ex99-1.htm). Same company, a different document.

findings.finding: The reported quarter will likely land at or just above the Q4 guide. TTEK beat in Q3 (EPS $0.42 against $0.40 consensus, net revenue above guide), has raised FY26 guidance four straight times, and Q4 consensus of $0.47 already sits in the upper half of the $0.45-0.48 guide, so any beat lands inside what the company told the market to expect.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats were sold or barely bought in 2026: -3.94%, +1.41%, +3.02%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced: the consensus already sits in the upper half of the guide. It is filed so the panel sees the reported quarter is not where the move comes from.
findings.independence: Consensus from Earnings Whispers via finviz (shared with the bar).

findings.finding: TTEK's first annual guides have been conservative. The initial FY26 guide (2025-11-12) was EPS $1.40-1.55, about 50% growth, and the final FY26 guide is $1.56-1.59, above the top of that range. A similarly conservative first FY27 range could put its midpoint below a thin $1.74-1.76 consensus, the 2-analyst, disputed bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last first-guide print, 2025-11-12, rose 15.29%: the market bought that conservative guide (Motley Fool called it 'superb'). That argues against this finding's sign and is why it is small with a wide band.
findings.why_not_priced: FY27 consensus is a thin aggregate ($1.71-1.76 across three aggregators, one of them on 2 analysts). A conservative first guide against it is a real, unpriced risk only if the market has forgotten how TTEK guides, and the last time it was not punished.
findings.independence: FY27 estimates: KeyBanc $1.74 (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/what-is-keycorps-forecast-for-tetra-tech-fy2027-earnings-2026-04-16/). Burdick on the Q3 call put FY27 margin expansion at about 50bp, 'a bit lower or higher' (Fool transcript, shared with the Ukraine finding).

outside_window.finding: The federal continuing resolution expires 2026-12-11. A lapse would hit Q1 FY27 federal billing, but the event itself is after the window (only the guide's treatment of it is in the window, filed above).

EPA's proposed extension of the PFOA/PFOS compliance deadline from 2029 to 2031 and rescission of the other four PFAS standards (proposed 2026-05-20, finalisation expected in 2026) slows municipal PFAS treatment demand. No final rule was found by 2026-11-11.

baseline_tension: What I found agrees with the skew (downside paid) and fades the 20-day run-up only through positioning. Fundamentally, the federal bookings read from Parsons and the buyback point mildly up, and the reported quarter is priced, so the lean rests mostly on reaction history and run-up, not on an unpriced number.
lessons_applied: Rule 5 (documents beat inference; none of what paid was weather): Hurricane Isaias finding cut from +0.3 to +0.1
Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction; this name's 2026 beats were sold or barely bought): reported-quarter beat finding cut from +0.3 to +0.1
Rule 3 (own caveat reaches the number: the last first-guide print rose 15.3% on a conservative guide): guidance-conservatism finding cut from -0.3 to -0.2
Rule 6 (disputed FY27 bar, 2 analysts and three aggregator values): guidance findings were already capped small and left there
Rule 7 (short interest checked first: ~4.5-4.8% of float, 4.8 days, not crowded; the negative agrees with the skew): positioning finding left at -1.0
abs_move_pct 7.0 and p_up 46 unchanged; post-lessons impact_sum -1.4 against -1.1 pre
